subject: EU/UK transfer mechanism — SCC module selection & execution plan (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acmehealth.com>, Juniper Privacy <privacy@juniperlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: SCC module clarification for Acme -> Redwood transfers

Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our procurement checklist we need to confirm which Standard Contractual Clauses module Redwood intends to execute for cross-border transfers from Acme (EU data controller) to Redwood (US-based processor). Our legal team has flagged the following open items:  

- Which SCC module will Redwood adopt (Module 2, Module 3, or a combination) given Redwood's role as an inference provider?
- Will Redwood execute the UK Addendum separately for UK-origin personal data?
- Can you provide a signed DPA + executed SCCs (DocuSign) and a SOC 2 snapshot as evidence?
- Are there any special subprocessors that would trigger Module 3 language for onward transfers?

We are on a compressed procurement timeline and would like to close contracts by 11/12. Please advise next steps and whether you need anything from our side (e.g., controller declarations, list of processing categories).

Thanks,
Alice Sullivan
Head of Compliance, Acme Health
Attachments: acme-sccs-questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 128KB)
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SCC module clarification for Acme -> Redwood transfers

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood operates as a processor for hosted inference, so our default approach is Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) for EU transfers plus execution of the UK Addendum for UK-origin data.  

A few important caveats we should confirm:  
- If Acme requires Redwood to engage an onward subprocessor that itself receives EU personal data and acts as a processor, we may need Module Three language for that specific subprocess.
- For Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC/air-gapped), contractual footprint is similar but we can surface a BAA discussion separately if required for HIPAA-covered PHI.

I've looped in Markus (legal) to review specific clause text and any redlines, and Irene (security/compliance) to attach SOC 2 evidence and DPIA notes. Our proposed next steps:  
1) Markus to confirm final module selection and produce redlined SCC + DPA for DocuSign.
2) Irene to attach SOC2 summary and data-flow DPIA notes.
3) We send executed docs via DocuSign and capture signed copies in the deal record.

Target: get executed DPA + SCCs by 11/12; we'll confirm exact DocuSign link in the next message.

—Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Sullivan <alice.sullivan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Juniper Privacy <privacy@juniperlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 13:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SCC module clarification for Acme -> Redwood transfers

Thanks Vanessa and Alice. Confirming legal position and proposed redlines:  

- Role confirmation: Redwood will be a Processor under the DPA; Acme is the Controller. That supports Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) for EU transfers.
- UK Addendum: we will execute the UK Addendum in parallel; the UK template requires a small addendum signature page which we include in the DocuSign envelope.
- Subprocessors: standard approach — we list known subprocessors in Annex II and provide 30 days notice of new subprocessors. Where Acme requires prior approval for a named subprocessor, we can negotiate specific additions. Onward transfers to subprocessors that process data as processors do not generally require Module Three, but if Redwood were to act as controller for a specific data stream (rare), we'd re-evaluate.

Attached: redlined-sccs-proposal.pdf (high-level redlines: narrow clause on security measures; explicit audit rights; retention cap of 90 days for temp logs). Action items for Acme legal: confirm whether you need a broader audit window or any bespoke controller obligations.

I will prepare the DPA + SCCs bundle and send via DocuSign for signature once Acme confirms the redline which is marked in the attached PDF. If we need to provide Annex II populated with subprocessors before signature, please let us know.

—Markus Klein
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlined-sccs-proposal.pdf (pdf, 62KB)

Subject: Re: SCC module clarification for Acme -> Redwood transfers — security evidence

Hi all,

Attaching the evidence pack requested by Acme. Key items included:  
- SOC 2 snapshot (SOC2-summary-2026.pdf): scope covers Redwood API and hosted inference runtime; there are no open exceptions.
- Data-flow & DPIA notes (data-flow-dpia-notes.docx): maps where Acme data will transit and retention behavior for inference artifacts.
- Note on HIPAA: for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment with a BAA; our standard hosted offering can be used for deidentified data or with contractual safeguards, but Acme should confirm whether the data set contains PHI.

Quick answers:  
- SOC2 evidence: provided as a summary here; we can share the full report under NDA if required.
- DPIA: early notes indicate that where Acme routes patient identifiers into inference requests, Acme should complete a DPIA and we can assist with our processing descriptions.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the technical annex if helpful.

—Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

1) Module selection: Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) is the baseline. UK Addendum will be executed alongside the EU SCCs.
2) Documents going out for signature: DPA (draft attached), EU SCCs bundle (redlined per Markus), UK Addendum.
3) Evidence: SOC2 summary + DPIA notes from Irene attached. We can provide the full SOC2 under NDA.
4) DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/REPLACE_WITH_ACME_DOCUSIGN_LINK (envelope will include the DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum).
5) Timeline: we will send the envelope EOD today if Acme confirms redlines; target fully executed by 2026-11-12.

Checklist for Acme to confirm:  
- Confirm Acme remains Controller for this engagement (yes/no).
- Confirm whether Acme requires prior approval for any of our listed subprocessors or if the standard 30-day notice is acceptable.
- Confirm whether the data set includes PHI that would require a BAA or Dedicated deployment option.

If you confirm these three items, we will send the DocuSign envelope immediately. Thanks — looking forward to closing and getting you onboarded.

Best,
Vanessa
